title: Affine weakly contractible covering family on the pro-etale site
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Every object $U$ of this site admits a covering family $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ in which each $U_i$ is affine and weakly contractible for the full site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Here weakly contractible means that for every epimorphism $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets on this site, $F(U_i)\to G(U_i)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0990, lemma-proetale-enough-w-contractible, small-site assertion; Tag 098I, lemma-get-many-weakly-contractible; sites.tex Tag 090L, definition-w-contractible, with Tag 090K, lemma-w-contractible, condition (2)

proof.text: Let $u:U\to X$ be the object in the statement. Choose an arbitrary affine open cover $U=\bigcup_{j\in J}T_j$, writing $T_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j$. The affine basis property follows from the locally affine definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]: restrict an affine chart around each point to principal opens contained in a prescribed neighborhood. Take $J$ to be a set of such opens of the $\mathcal U$-small scheme $U$. There is no finiteness assertion for $J$.

For each $j$ choose an infinite $\mathcal U$-small cardinal $\kappa_j\geq |A_j|$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-ring-extension] to obtain $A_j\to D_j$, and set $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}D_j$ with the induced map $p_j:V_j\to T_j$. Retain all clauses: $p_j$ is a one-member pro-etale covering, $D_j$ has the splitting property, and $|D_j|\leq\kappa_j^{2^{2^{2^{\kappa_j}}}}$.

The bound in step 2 is $\mathcal U$-small: Grothendieck universes are closed under power sets and function sets, so the iterated powers and cardinal exponentiation remain below the universe bound [def-weil-size-convention]. Replace $D_j$ by an isomorphic ring on a subset of a set of that bounded cardinality. Its prime ideals are subsets of $D_j$, and the topology and structure sheaf are built from subsets, localizations (quotients of pairs), and sets of functions; all these sets lie in $\mathcal U$. Hence $V_j$ is a $\mathcal U$-small affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The family indexed by $J$ is formed inside $\mathcal V$. Use representatives in the chosen skeleton, conjugating every map by the representing isomorphisms. This uses the bounded witness explicitly, rather than an arbitrary existential witness.

proof.text: The open immersion $i_j:T_j\to U$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Its diagonal is an isomorphism: the fibre product of an open subset with itself over $U$ is that open subset, by the open-subscheme definition [def-weil-open-immersion]. An isomorphism is flat since its local-ring maps are isomorphisms. Thus $i_j$ is weakly etale by [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], $p_j$ is weakly etale and the composites $i_jp_j$ and $u i_jp_j$ are weakly etale. Step 3 and the definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] now make $V_j\to X$ an object of the full small site and $V_j\to U$ a morphism there.

source.place: Tag 098I, lemma-get-many-weakly-contractible, construction; composition: more-morphisms.tex Tag 094T, lemma-composition-weakly-etale

proof.text: Fix an affine open $W\subseteq U$. Cover $W$ by affine opens $W_a$ subordinate to the open cover $(W\cap T_j)_j$: the affine basis gives $W_a\subseteq W\cap T_{j(a)}$. The affine scheme $W$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so finitely many of these OPEN subsets $W_a$ cover $W$. Apply the one-member covering clause of [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-ring-extension] to $p_{j(a)}$ and the affine open $W_a\subseteq T_{j(a)}$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] gives finitely many affine opens $Z_{a,b}\subseteq V_{j(a)}$ whose images under $p_{j(a)}$ have union exactly $W_a$. Taking all these finitely many $Z_{a,b}$, their images under the composites have union $W$. Together with step 4 this is precisely the pro-etale covering criterion for $(V_j\to U)_j$. Neither $W\cap T_j$ nor an arbitrary image upstairs is assumed affine or open. If $W$ is empty, take no witnesses.

source.place: Tag 098I, lemma-get-many-weakly-contractible; Tag 0989, definition-fpqc-covering; affine quasi-compactness: algebra.tex Tag 00E8, lemma-quasi-compact

proof.text: For each $j$, the splitting clause for $D_j$ from [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-ring-extension] and the already verified full-site object $V_j\to X$ satisfy all hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-wcontractible-affine-weakly-contractible]. Therefore every sheaf epimorphism $F\to G$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is surjective on evaluation at $V_j$. Each $V_j$ is affine, and step 5 gives a covering family in this same site. This proves the requested statement for arbitrary $U$. The empty object is covered by the empty family.
